packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-07 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: No proposed identification of the work or author was in my context. The only text beyond the script that I saw is modern pencil labels on the fragments themselves ("STA, Fap. 102-1r" ... "102-4r", "102-1v" ... "102-4v" on the reverse). I did nothing beyond the reader brief: I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..014 in this packet (plus the packet-08 materials named to me separately). I listed the packet directory to find the image filenames; I did not open packet.json.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 (overview, face 1) and image-008 (overview, face 2): four separate parchment scraps laid side by side, upright. Left to right on face 1: fragment A (smallest, labelled 102-4r), B (narrow strip, 102-3r), C (largest, with transparent repair tape and black stains, 102-2r), D (102-1r). On face 2 the order is the same (4v, 3v, 2v, 1v).
- Single column of text on each scrap as visible; all are cut on at least two sides, so full column width and the number of columns per page are unknown.
- Gothic textualis/cursiva-type small book hand, heavily abbreviated. Red stroked capitals (touched letters) at sentence starts; red-flourished or red initials (e.g. a red V on C 2r).
- Rubrics: on C (2r) a boxed and red-underlined heading "De modo viuendi"; on D (1r) a red-underlined heading "Profundu(m) triplex" and lower a faded heading "De tribus diet(is)?" with a second rubric line, both crossed/underlined in red.
- Fragments A and B are cleaner and in a slightly different, more upright and larger hand/ink than C and D (observation only; may or may not be the same manuscript).
- Fragment A face 2 (4v) is mostly blank/abraded in the middle; it shows ends of lines of a left column at the left edge and beginnings of lines of a right column at the right edge, i.e. this scrap seems to come from the intercolumn area of a two-column page (tentative). A few faint words lie in the middle area (possibly a marginal/intercolumnar addition).
- No interlinear glosses noticed except small superscript corrections/abbreviations.

SELECTED SPANS: all four scraps on both faces, reading every line where possible. Left and right line ends are cut on every scrap; I mark the cut as [...].
Overlaps: image-002 shows only the tops of A and B (same lines as image-005 lines 1-2); image-003/006 overlap on C (image-006 lines 1-3 = image-003 lines 13-15); image-004/007 overlap on D (image-007 lines 1-3 = image-004 lines 12-14). Same pattern on face 2 (009/012, 010/013, 011/014). I number lines from each image's top and do not repeat overlap lines as new text.

FACE 1
=====================================================
